evidence: Authored for this product: instruction.md:1-17 is a first-person HireOps brief (pipeline board per job plus recruiter-candidate conversations, multi-user non-trampling as the stated 'hard part'); hireops_rules.md:1-209 defines HireOps-specific mechanics (six stages with Rejected aside, per-job interview places 1-50, hiring-manager late-stage scope, per-card version 409 naming the colleague, all-or-none bulk move ordered by board order, single-level undo invalidated by later card changes but not notes, 30-message paging that preserves the top message, per-person unread/seen rules where the Observer never counts, per-person per-browser drafts surviving session end, candidate wording table and candidate data redaction). Seed (environment/assets/seed_data.json) is coherent recruiting data (JOB-PLAT/JOB-DATA/JOB-DSGN, APP-1xx, candidate accounts). All functional criteria use task-specific hro_* ids and HireOps names (e.g. functional/judge.toml hro_restart quotes the seeded Platform Engineer order; hro_seen distinguishes Observer vs candidate/manager opens); polish (hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_earlier_place, hro_pol_session_resume) and visual (hro_vis_type names board, conversations and activity) are product-specific, and the template's six generic visual_* ids were not copied verbatim. A grep of the whole frozen task for sibling product names/nouns (torquebay, pellmoor, docketlight, bazaar, boardloom, colderwater, ridgeline, drawbill, threadline, gridforge, patchpad, work order, SKU, vacancy, canvas, invoice, storefront, cart) found only the ordinary word 'claims' at hireops_rules.md:12, so no leftover renamed-sibling text. Sibling comparison: the closest sibling is projects/pellmoor-job-pipeline (also recruiting). Shared ideas are generic domain rules (no stage skipping, a capacity cap, stale 409, atomic batch), but Pellmoor's core flows are panels/scores, assessment-version freshness, offer-opening capacity, actor-scoped durable retry receipts and a d3 history-derived funnel (hiring-rules.md:1-121), while HireOps' core flows are live multi-user board convergence without disturbing focus/drafts/scroll, manual shared ordering, undo, conversations with paging/unread/seen/drafts and a candidate portal; Pellmoor has no messaging, undo, ordering, candidate login or live updates, and HireOps has no panels, scores, funnel or receipts. Criteria sets do not correspond one-to-one. Pellmoor is also a retired dimensions-layout task (tests/reward.toml) with a different stack slice. threadline-chat shares paging/unread concepts but is a channel chat (threads, reactions, mentions, edit/delete, search) with no pipeline board or candidate side. torquebay is a repair-shop desk. So HireOps is not a nouns-swapped clone. Domain-plan fit: NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:203 requires distinct domain behaviour reusing infrastructure; task.toml provenance says 'Adapted from the supplied HireOps task as a recruiting workspace', i.e. an assigned product, and its description/keywords/difficulty_explanation accurately describe it (line 82 guidance). Minor observation, not a defect for this row: arena_slice = "recruiting-hiring-operations" (task.toml:15) does not follow the stack-prefixed convention most siblings use (e.g. full-stack-node-express-sqlite-...); the staged contract (staged-task-contract.md task.toml block) only requires a value, so I record no failure. No suite-level domain-plan document assigning slices exists in the workspace, so 'fits the domain plan' is judged against the assignment provenance and the absence of overlap; a second recruiting task in the suite (Pellmoor) is a domain overlap but with distinct mechanics. Adversarial angle: this row grades task authorship, not app behaviour, so a broken or conforming app cannot change its outcome; the realistic failure (renamed sibling flows/criteria) was checked and not found.
